text: This project is about live research agents whose results get verified. Each week, three agents find new forecasting claims, check them against their sources, and measure them on our own data.

Our test case is electricity load. Demand is growing, partly because of data centers, and foundation models for time series are improving fast. A disclaimer: week-ahead load forecasting is a well-known problem, and we are not trying to beat power providers or energy hedge funds. These forecasts run fast enough for a hackathon, and they show weather doing real work.
Grid operators schedule power plants from a forecast of demand, called load. PJM is the largest in the United States, and forecast error there is real money.
Our test bed is four PJM zones: Jersey Central and Dominion, then AEP and Atlantic City Electric, kept back for a fresh test.
Every Monday, each method forecasts the next 168 hours in four PJM zones. Every method gets the same history and the same temperature forecast, and the rules were frozen before any scored run.

Here is a receipt. A study found that in Great Britain, Chronos-2 roughly ties a regression: a ratio of 0.97. Against our first baseline we measured 0.73 on Dominion, a clear win. But against the field's standard benchmark it is 0.95: close to a tie again.
So we ran a fresh test on two zones no model had been run on, with everything fixed in advance: 1.01 and 0.89. Neither clears our ten percent bar.

The leaderboard shows every model against the same baseline, two zones side by side. The grey diamonds, Timestral and TimesFM 3.0, were published after most of our test weeks, so their scores are not out of sample.
Weather matters more than the model. With better weather forecasts every method improves, and the regressions catch up with Chronos-2.
Each week, two scans look for new claims: one with Claude's built-in search, one with You.com. Combined, they found sixty.

With You.com, every result carries a date, and a search can be limited to one site and an exact date range. It kept fifty-three claims against forty-four. And on the six claims judged both ways, the verdicts were the same.
With Open Crawl, a code review could also search the project's history, and it recovered why the agents were built this way.
Find, judge, run, receipt. Receipts, not hype. The voice in this video is A.I. generated.
